children: Crude and refined product contracts were a mixed bag by midday Tuesday, regaining their footing following three straight sessions of sharp pullbacks as the market was digesting President Trump's remarks about Iran.
At 11:55 a.m. ET, more-active November NYMEX West Texas Intermediate crude futures were down about 65cts to $91.70/bbl and October WTI was up around 30cts to $96.05/bbl.
London-based December ICE Brent was down 15cts to $100.20/bbl and January Brent was 10cts lower to $96.10/bbl.
November NYMEX ULSD was up about 1ct to $4.7715/gal and October ULSD was 0.2ct lower to $4.8690/gal. November RBOB was 3.9cts higher to $3.2375/gal and October RBOB was 4.45cts higher to $3.5145/gal.

During his remarks to the United Nations, Trump renewed his threats with strong rhetoric against Iran. However, Trump said he still expects Tehran to make a deal after the November midterm elections in the U.S.
